label: 0040 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over all windows of 0024): 0039 with time-varying Hokkaido block rotations after Tokachi-oki, correlated noise, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0039 with time-varying rotations of the okhotsk and kuril-north blocks after the 2003 Tokachi-oki earthquake: a decaying rigid motion of each block (prior 10 mm/yr in the first year, Omori decay with c = 10 yr), estimated with the static rotations from the 1997–2011 windows. In 0039 the static rotations still carried part of the post-Tokachi-oki transient; now it goes into the departures, about 8–11 mm/yr in the first month, 2–4 mm/yr in 2006–2015 and 1–2 mm/yr after 2018. The static Hokkaido rotations move 2–3 mm/yr back west (kuril-north −2.6 mm/yr east against −0.8 in 0039; okhotsk +0.9 against +2.6), and the Hokkaido residual RMS before 2003 drops from 5.5 to 5.1 mm/yr. On synthetic data the departures recover 97–99% of a planted decaying block motion, of which 6 of 10 mm/yr went into the static rotations without them. Window cross-validation is 10.5 above 0039's and higher in 26 of 33 windows; it can't tell this block answer from 0039's, because it scores with the same correlated noise that makes island-wide offsets cheap. The correlated-noise level of 0038–0040 is the cross-validation optimum. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
